coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Chase Center
record.summary: An 18,064-to-19,500-seat arena for the Golden State Warriors (NBA) and Golden State Valkyries (WNBA, since 2025), anchoring an 11-acre, privately financed mixed-use development in Mission Bay with 580,000 sq ft of office/lab space (leased in full by Uber as its San Francisco headquarters since 2022), 100,000 sq ft of retail ("Thrive City") and a 35,000 sq ft public plaza; designed by MANICA Architecture with Gensler (interiors), built by a Mortenson/Clark Construction joint venture, and opened September 6, 2019.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL, DERIVED BOUNDARY -- the outer edge is a real DataSF Assessor Parcel boundary (blklot 8722025); the two notches cut into its NW and SW corners are real OpenStreetMap building traces (the Uber towers), not estimates. The resulting shape has not been independently verified against a surveyed Chase Center site plan -- it is real-minus-real, not a single authoritative source. Two small structures inside this polygon (an oval building in the west plaza, and possibly others) remain unidentified as of this pass. street_clip_exempt is set: the real-street centerline layer (src/street_geometry.py) shows several stale/closed street segments cutting straight through the arena bowl itself (visible as a literal cross running under the roof in a direct render against the street buffer) -- leftover records from the four separate plan blocks (29/30/31/32) that were consolidated into one superblock when Chase Center was built, not real current streets. Auto-clipping against them removed 16% of this polygon's real area; exempted per the same documented-reason precedent as Pier 70's 20th Street Plaza.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor Parcel blklot 8722025 (Mission Bay South Blocks 29-32), with the two Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 office-tower footprints (real OpenStreetMap building outlines, OSM ways 1410182008 and 1410183655) subtracted out -- see digitization_method.

Executive Director Bohee reported that OCII was the respondent along with the City and others 
in litigation filed by the Mission Bay Alliance regarding the Warriors Arena Project.  She 
announced that the previous day the California Superior Court had upheld the subsequent 
Environmental Impact Report which had been certified by OCII.

Ms. Bohee expected that the 
Golden State Warriors would be coming back to the Commission in coming months for 
approval of their comprehensive signage package and at that time would provide an update on 
the SBE, local hire, art, design, etc.

RESOLUTION NO. 14-2026, APPROVING A SIXTH AMENDMENT TO THE MISSION BAY SOUTH SIGNAGE MASTER PLAN INCREASING CHARACTER HEIGHTS AND FLEXIBILITY OF AWNING SIGNS FOR MIXED USE RETAIL USES AND FOR THE EVENT CENTER SIGN PROGRAM AT THE GOLDEN STATE WARRIORS EVENT CENTER AND MIXED-USE DEVELOPMENT ON BLOCKS 29-32 IN MISSION BAY SOUTH; MISSION BAY SOUTH REDEVELOPMENT PROJECT AREA, BE ADOPTED.

Miller & Lux, a 7,000 sq ft, two-floor steakhouse from chef Tyler Florence (designed by Ken Fulk), opened Sept 28, 2021 at 7 Warriors Way Ste 208 in Thrive City -- named after Henry Miller and Charles Lux, meatpacking-district butchers who once occupied the arena's site.

Cupcakin' Bake Shop opened at 7 Warriors Way Unit 200 in Thrive City on Oct 18, 2022, its fifth Bay Area location (after two in Berkeley, one in Oakland, one in Walnut Creek), adjacent to the Warriors Team Shop.
Siren Cafe & Bar, a seafood-focused cafe and bar from Michael Iglesias and Joseph Cleveland of Dos Ojos Hospitality, opened as a pop-up at Thrive City around February 2025.

The Sarap Shop, a Filipino-American food business from Kristen Brillantes, JP Reyes and James Brillantes (previously a food truck, with a flagship in SOMA Pilipinas), operates a stand at 1 Warriors Way in Thrive City; no specific opening date found.
Dumpling Time opened at 191 Warriors Way on Feb 3, 2020, the first restaurant to open in Thrive City, the retail plaza surrounding Chase Center.
b8ta, which opened a storefront at Thrive City in January 2020, closed along with every other b8ta store in the US on Feb 18, 2022, citing pandemic foot traffic and a rise in burglaries.
Harmonic Brewing opened its second location, a taproom with a 2,000 sq ft waterfront patio, at 7 Warriors Way Suite 206 in Thrive City, with regular hours starting May 17, 2021.
Gott's Roadside opened a 4,000 sq ft restaurant at 1 Warriors Way in Thrive City on Sep 17, 2021, its seventh Bay Area location and second in San Francisco.
Mission Bay Wine Bar opened an extension of its Channel Street shop at Thrive City on Jan 31, 2023; its Yelp listing now shows the Thrive City location as closed, though no closure date was found.
Che Fico Pizzeria, from chef David Nayfeld and Matt Brewer of Back Home Hospitality, opened at Thrive City on Oct 9, 2024, with sweeping bay views and a walk-up gelato window.
Fikscue Craft Barbecue, known for Indonesian-Texas barbecue fusion, opened to the public at Thrive City's Esplanade on June 12, 2025.
Splash at Thrive City, a two-story, 30,000 sq ft sports bar from Sidecar Hospitality (Pacific Cocktail Haven), opened Feb 7, 2025, ahead of NBA All-Star and Super Bowl weekend.
Chase Center gained its first two photos -- an exterior and an interior arena shot -- having had zero images of any kind before this.

Chase Center promoted from an orientation-only landmark to a tracked record on its real, active parcel (blklot 8722025). The landmark row it replaces had pointed at blklot 8722001, a retired/superseded Assessor parcel -- not caught until this pass cross-checked it against a fresh parcel fetch.

open_questions: 2026-09-23: this record's geometry was migrated off status.csv (record_id changed from the blklot '8722025' to 'mission_bay_chase_center') because DataSF's own Assessor Parcel dataset gives this parcel and the neighboring Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 towers byte-identical geometry (one shared master-condo superblock parcel). The new geometry is the full Assessor parcel with both Uber towers' own real OSM building footprints subtracted out -- see the geojson's own digitization_method. Two small structures inside the resulting polygon are not yet identified: an oval building in the west plaza, and possibly others not yet checked against a satellite pass.

Chase Center's final cost is genuinely disputed in reporting: $1.4B is the most-repeated figure (Construction Dive), but a Warriors executive (Rick Welts, per Wikipedia) put the actual final cost closer to $1.3B after a roughly 30% overrun from an original budget. A separate 2019 Construction Dive piece on the (distinct, unbuilt) hotel/condo proposal used '$1.5B Chase Center' in its own headline, which appears to conflate the arena with that proposal; that figure is not used here.
Uber's exact current headcount or lease status as of 2026 was not independently verified; the source describing its 584,000-586,000 sq ft lease is from January 2022.

The Warriors-proposed hotel/condo/retail complex on adjacent Blocks 29-30 is financially and physically tied to Chase Center but may sit on a separate parcel; whether it falls within blklot 8722025 or is a distinct, not-yet-built record is not confirmed. Current 2026 construction status is also unconfirmed.

No primary Port of San Francisco or OCII page dedicated specifically to Chase Center was found (as a privately financed project, it may not have one); the only agency-level source found was SFPUC/CleanPowerSF's sustainability write-up.
No openly licensed image was found; recommend linking rather than hosting until one is confirmed.
